instructions:
# How to translate this chunk

This file holds `items`, a list of `{"k", "ctx", "t"}`. `t` is English text
that a reader of an Indian app or website sees. `ctx` is the field it came
from, such as label, hint, button, documents, brief or title. Use it to judge
tone and length: a label stays short, a hint can be a sentence.

Write `{"items": [{"k": ..., "t": ...}, ...]}` to the path in `write_to`.
Keep every `k` unchanged and in the same order. Put the translation in `t`.
Leave out `ctx`. Do not add, merge, split or drop items.

## Keep these exactly as they are

- Placeholders and markup: `{0}`, `{name}`, `%s`, `%d`, `%1$s`, HTML tags, `\n`.
- Website addresses, e-mail addresses and links.
- Every number: phone and toll-free numbers, Aadhaar, account, IFSC, PAN, PIN
  codes, amounts, dates, percentages. Write digits as 0-9, the Western digits,
  in every language, including Urdu. People type these into forms that take
  Western digits.
- Acronyms people know in Latin letters: OTP, PAN, IFSC, UPI, KYC, e-KYC, DBT,
  BPL, APL, NFSA, PM-KISAN, SMS, PDF, ID.

## Names

- Product, app, portal and scheme names: transliterate them into the script so
  they read naturally. Keep any acronym inside them in Latin, so "APPSC
  portal" becomes APPSC followed by the word for portal.
- A button or menu label quoted from a website, such as 'Apply Online' or
  'Register', stays in English inside quotes. The reader has to find that exact
  English word on the screen.
- People and places in examples are transliterated, never replaced with other
  names.
- Government office titles are transliterated so the reader can say them at
  the counter: Tahsildar, Patwari, Talathi, Mamlatdar, BDO, Collector, Gram
  Panchayat. The language notes below give the usual local forms.

## Tone

Write for an ordinary person who may be elderly and may have had little
schooling. Use everyday spoken language, not heavy official vocabulary. Where
people really say the English word, write it in the script: online, form,
portal, login, mobile, bank, certificate, download, upload, app. Keep
instructions short and direct, in the form "do this".

"Gender" means sex (male or female). It is never the word for caste.

## Before you write

Check that you have the same number of items as the input and that every
number and placeholder came through. Write the whole file in ONE Write call,
as valid UTF-8 JSON with no `\u` escapes and nothing else in the file.

## Hindi (hi)

Script: Devanagari. Used in UP, MP, Bihar, Rajasthan, Haryana, HP, Uttarakhand,
Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh and Delhi, and understood across the north.
Tone: everyday spoken Hindi (Hindustani). Avoid Sanskritised official words.
Words: ऑनलाइन, फॉर्म, पोर्टल, लॉगिन, आधार, बैंक, मोबाइल, OTP, हेल्पलाइन,
सर्टिफिकेट, डाउनलोड, अपलोड.
UI: आवेदन करें (Apply), जमा करें (Submit), आगे (Next), पीछे (Back), खोजें (Search),
शेयर करें (Share), सेटिंग (Settings), भाषा (Language), मदद (Help).
Offices: तहसीलदार, पटवारी, ग्राम पंचायत, कलेक्टर, ब्लॉक विकास कार्यालय (BDO).
Gender: लिंग (never जाति). Money: रु. 6,000; रु. 8 लाख. September: सितंबर.

Words: ઓનલાઇન, ફોર્મ, પોર્ટલ, લૉગિન, આધાર, બેંક, મોબાઇલ, OTP, હેલ્પલાઇન, સર્ટિફિકેટ / દાખલો,
ડાઉનલોડ, અપલોડ.

Offices: મામલતદાર, તલાટી, ગ્રામ પંચાયત, કલેક્ટર, તાલુકા પંચાયત.

Words: ऑनलाइन, फॉर्म, पोर्टल, लॉगिन, आधार, बँक, मोबाइल, OTP, हेल्पलाइन, दाखला / सर्टिफिकेट,
डाउनलोड, अपलोड.

## Bengali (bn)

Script: Bengali. Used in West Bengal and Tripura, and in Assam's Barak Valley

Tone: everyday spoken Bengali (চলিত ভাষা), not সাধু ভাষা.
Words: অনলাইন, ফর্ম, পোর্টাল, লগইন, আধার, ব্যাংক, মোবাইল, OTP, হেল্পলাইন, সার্টিফিকেট,
ডাউনলোড, আপলোড.
UI: আবেদন করুন, জমা দিন, পরবর্তী, পিছনে, খুঁজুন, শেয়ার করুন, সেটিংস, ভাষা, সাহায্য.

## Assamese (as)

Script: Bengali script with the Assamese letters ৰ and ৱ. Used in Assam.
This is Assamese, not Bengali. Use Assamese words and spellings: আঁচনি
(scheme), বেংক (bank), কৰক (do), নহয় (is not).
Words: অনলাইন, প্ৰপত্ৰ / ফৰ্ম, পৰ্টেল, লগইন, আধাৰ, বেংক, মবাইল, OTP, হেল্পলাইন, প্ৰমাণপত্ৰ,
ডাউনল'ড, আপল'ড.
UI: আবেদন কৰক, দাখিল কৰক, পৰৱৰ্তী, উভতি যাওক, বিচাৰক, শ্বেয়াৰ কৰক, ছেটিংছ, ভাষা, সহায়.
Offices: চক্ৰ বিষয়াৰ কাৰ্যালয় (Circle Office), গাঁও পঞ্চায়ত, উন্নয়ন খণ্ড কাৰ্যালয় (BDO),
জিলা উপায়ুক্ত.
Gender: লিংগ. Money: 6,000 টকা; 8 লাখ টকা. September: ছেপ্তেম্বৰ.

## Punjabi (pa)

Mukhyamantri Ladli Laxmi Yojana (Ladli Laxmi 2.0)
Department of Women and Child Development, Madhya Pradesh

When a girl is born in Madhya Pradesh and registered under this scheme, the state issues a certificate in her name promising Rs 1,43,000 in stages. She gets scholarships when she joins classes 6, 9, 11 and 12, Rs 25,000 when she joins college, and Rs 1 lakh at age 21. The state also pays her college tuition fees. Parents should apply within one year of her birth, either online themselves or through the anganwadi.
Rs 1,43,000 in stages: Rs 18,000 school scholarships, Rs 25,000 for college, Rs 1 lakh at 21
Girl born on or after 1 January 2006 and registered at the local anganwadi centre
Parents are original residents of Madhya Pradesh and do not pay income tax
Parents have two children or fewer. The first girl qualifies without any condition. For the second girl, the mother or father must have adopted family planning after the second child
Apply within one year of the girl's birth. Late cases, orphans, adopted girls and girls who have lost a parent can be registered up to age 5 as special cases
The final Rs 1 lakh is paid only if she has appeared for the class 12 exam and was not married before 18
Samagra family ID, with the girl added as a member and her 9-digit Samagra member ID
Photo of the girl with her mother or father (JPG or PNG, 40 to 200 KB)
Family planning (sterilisation) certificate, if this is the second girl
Aadhaar card of the mother or father, with e-KYC done in Samagra

Mahatma Jyotirao Phule Jan Arogya Yojana (MJPJAY / Ayushman Card)
Public Health Department, Government of Maharashtra (State Health Assurance Society)

Free, cashless hospital treatment for every family in Maharashtra, up to Rs.5 lakh a family each year, at government and private hospitals that have joined the scheme. Since 1 July 2024 it runs together with the central Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY, so one Ayushman card works for both, and families with a white ration card, or with no ration card but a Maharashtra domicile certificate, are covered as well. It was earlier called Rajiv Gandhi Jeevandayee Arogya Yojana. There is nothing to apply for in advance: at the hospital, the Arogyamitra desk registers the patient with the ration card and Aadhaar.
Rs.5 lakh a year per family, cashless, at network hospitals
Every family living in Maharashtra, whatever its income (universal cover since 1 July 2024)
Families with a yellow, Antyodaya (AAY), Annapurna, orange or white ration card
A family with no ration card is covered if it holds a Maharashtra domicile certificate
The Rs.5 lakh is shared by the whole family in a year (family floater), and illnesses you already have are covered from the first day
Covers listed surgeries and hospital treatments in 34 specialities at network hospitals in Maharashtra; in 2025 the state approved widening the list from 1,356 to 2,399 procedures
Ration card of any colour (yellow, orange, white, AAY or Annapurna)
Aadhaar card of the patient
Maharashtra domicile certificate, if the family has no ration card

Ayushman card, if already made (it is not needed to start treatment)

The Arogyamitra desk at any MJPJAY network (empanelled) hospital in Maharashtra, government or private; it is usually near the main reception. The Ayushman card itself can be made beforehand at a CSC (Aaple Sarkar Seva Kendra), through the ASHA worker, or at the same hospital desk.

When a doctor says the patient needs an operation or admission, ask whether the hospital is an MJPJAY / Ayushman network hospital. If you are not sure, call 155388 or look up the hospital list on jeevandayee.gov.in.

The doctor examines the patient, and the hospital sends a pre-authorisation request online to the State Health Assurance Society with the reports. Approval usually comes within hours; in an emergency, treatment starts first.
Once approved, the listed treatment, operation, medicines, tests, bed and food are free. Do not pay cash or sign any paper promising to pay for a listed treatment.

To make the next visit quicker, get the Ayushman card made for every family member at a CSC, through the ASHA worker or at the Arogyamitra desk.

Sanjay Gandhi Niradhar Anudan Yojana (Niradhar Pension)
Social Justice and Special Assistance Department, Government of Maharashtra (through the Tehsildar)

A monthly pension of Rs.1,500 for people under 65 who have no one to support them: persons with 40% or more disability, people with serious illnesses such as cancer, TB, HIV or leprosy, widows, divorced or abandoned women, orphan children and transgender persons, among others. Disabled beneficiaries get Rs.2,500 a month from October 2025. The money comes every month by DBT into an Aadhaar-linked bank account. You apply through the talathi or the tehsil office; the state has also opened online applications on the MahaDBT portal.

Collect the papers first: income certificate from the tehsildar (apply at a Setu or Aaple Sarkar Seva Kendra), residence certificate, age proof and the proof of your category, such as the UDID card or husband's death certificate.
Get the form from the talathi, the tehsil office or a Setu kendra. Fill it in, sign or put your thumb impression in front of a witness, and attach the self-declaration with a photo.

Hand it to the talathi or at the tehsil's Sanjay Gandhi Yojana branch and take the acknowledgement. The talathi visits your home to check the papers and family income and uploads a photo of the visit.

The tehsildar checks the file and places it before the Sanjay Gandhi Niradhar Anudan Yojana committee, which meets every month. The lists of approved and rejected names are put on the notice board and read in the gram sabha.
Once approved, the pension starts from the month after the online process is complete and comes by DBT into your Aadhaar-linked account every month.

Keep your Aadhaar and bank linking in order, because payments that fail for Aadhaar or bank reasons are the beneficiary's responsibility. Give the life certificate each year when the tehsil asks; if the pension stopped, giving it in the same financial year restarts it.
If nothing happens for two or three months, go to the tehsil office with your acknowledgement and ask for the committee's decision.
Sanjay Gandhi Yojana branch of your tehsil office; 1800-120-8040 (Aaple Sarkar helpline)
Shravanbal Seva Rajya Nivruttivetan Yojana (Shravanbal Pension)

A monthly pension of Rs.1,500 for poor men and women aged 65 and above in Maharashtra. If the family is not on the BPL list but earns up to Rs.21,000 a year, the whole Rs.1,500 comes from the state (Group A). If the family is on the BPL list, the person gets the central Indira Gandhi old-age pension plus a Shravanbal top-up, again Rs.1,500 in all (Group B). Each eligible person is counted separately, so husband and wife can both get it, applying with one form each at the talathi or tehsil office; the money comes monthly by DBT.
